title: Habit and Success
excerpt: The greatest difference between success and failure comes from different habits.

inline.s: Excerpt from The Power of Habit
The greatest difference between success and failure comes from different habits.

In the final exams of my first semester at university, I failed several courses and sank to the verge of being expelled. I skipped classes, could barely read any book, and kept putting off my assignments until they were past the final deadline. I tried to make an effort and to change, but with little effect. At last, my grandfather called me before him and gave me a piece of earnest advice — and it was his counsel that changed my life.

blocks.text: There Are Two Kinds of People in the World

inline.s: My grandfather’s tone seemed to declare that every word he spoke could withstand scientific scrutiny and the test of time, that each was an indisputable, certain fact. It was this: people can be divided into two kinds — the dreamer and the doer (
Dreamer and Doer

“There are two kinds of people in the world: dreamers and doers,” my grandfather explained. “Dreamers are good at talking, imagining, longing, even planning to do great things; but doers do! Right now you are a dreamer — it seems that no matter how hard you try, you cannot bring yourself to accomplish the things you know you should do, or could do. But never mind; you can still turn yourself into a doer.”
These words of my grandfather changed my life from then on, and I believe they can change yours too.
So, if you are still only a dreamer, how can you become a doer? What exactly is this transformation, and how can it take place?

blocks.text: The Difference Between Dreamers and Doers

inline.s: First, let us look closely: what are dreamers and doers, and how do the two differ?
Doers succeed more than dreamers because
doers consistently take persistent, purposeful action
, whereas dreamers seldom set to work, or having just begun, soon grow slack.
Doers possess the ability to change their lives with purpose.

They can accomplish extraordinary undertakings — whether founding their own company, writing a book, running for public office, entering a marathon, or other endeavors. In sharp contrast, dreamers merely stand to one side and do no more than dream of such things.

What prevents dreamers from achieving great things? Is it merely fear of “beginning”? Or worry about failure? Or is it that dreamers are not clever enough, lack wisdom, are deficient in ability, or have poor luck? And what exactly enables doers to act, and thereby accomplish satisfying undertakings, while dreamers are doomed to failure after failure? The answer is simple — and yet, profound.
What drives doers forward, and what likewise holds dreamers back, is one and the same thing: habit!
Who am I?
I am your lifelong companion, your best helper, and yet I may become your heaviest burden.
I can push you ever forward, or drag you down until you fail.
I obey you entirely, and of the things you do, more than half will be entrusted to me, for I can always carry out a task quickly and precisely.
I am easy to manage — so long as you discipline me strictly.
Tell me exactly how you want me to do it,
and after a few practices I will carry out the task automatically.
I am the servant of all great men, and, alas, the accomplice of all failures. The great are great because of my mighty aid; and for why the failures fail, my guilt is no less inescapable.

I am not a machine; besides working with a machine’s precision, I also possess human intelligence. You may use me to gain wealth, or you may be ruined because of me — to me the two are no different, for I am simply doing the work you trained me to do.
Seize me, train me, discipline me strictly, and I will lay the whole world at your feet. But never indulge me, for then I will destroy you!
I am Habit.
Excerpt from Habit Determines Success

Success is a habit, and failure is a habit too. Why does one succeed? Because of perseverance. Why does one fail? Because of slackness and giving up. Perseverance and giving up are both habits. Good habits are the mighty force that carries us toward success, so it is no wonder some say that the greatest difference between success and failure comes from different habits.
As habits grow from “seedlings” into “great trees,” the more often they are repeated and the longer they exist, the harder they are to change.
Who you are today is the result of your past habits; the habits you keep now are shaping the you of the future.

Change every habitual pattern that makes you unhappy and unsuccessful, and your destiny will change; the more wholesome and expansive your habit-field becomes, the freer and more vital your life will be, and the greater your accomplishments.

Success is sometimes not as difficult as one imagines: form one good habit every day and stick to it, and success may be just around the corner. Forming one good habit each day is easy; the hard part is persevering. This is a union of conviction and endurance, so it is hardly surprising that so few people succeed.
